title: RBAC V2 on-call surge procedure and postmortem template
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a hybrid on-call surge playbook and postmortem template specifically for incidents involving RBAC V2 (permission delegations, policy drift, anomalous role assignments) where audit logs and automated evidence exports are the primary forensic sources. It is intended for security on-call, incident commander, and SRE responders.

When to use this document:
- Any suspected or confirmed RBAC policy violation (unexpected privilege grants, mass role changes, delegation chains kicked off by automation).
- Suspicious login followed by privilege escalation steps.
- Alerts from SIEM that reference RBAC policy decisions (denied->allowed anomalies, cross-account role use).

Quick-reference surge checklist (first 15 minutes):
1) Triage & visibility
   - Confirm alert source (SIEM, telemetry, external report). Note ID and time.
   - If high-likelihood: page sec-oncall and declare a surge.
   - Assign Incident Commander (IC) and Evidence Owner.
2) Contain immediate blast radius
   - If actor is a service account, disable keys/tokens or rotate ephemeral creds immediately.
   - For user accounts with active sessions, force session revocation where supported.
   - Apply temporary deny-rule for suspect role bindings (use RBAC V2 emergency policy template: emergency-deny-<incident-id>).
3) Preserve evidence (do NOT alter agents/hosts beyond containment)
   - Trigger automated evidence-collector job (see "Automation triggers" below).
   - Manually snapshot control-plane logs if automation fails (download last 72 hours of audit indexes).
4) Communication
   - Post a running incident note in #sec-oncall (incident id, summary, IC, next updates cadence).

RBAC V2 audit-log quick schema (fields to collect immediately):
- event_ts: ISO8601 timestamp of event
- request_id: unique request identifier (trace id)
- actor_id: user/service principal id (email/arn)
- actor_role: role(s) as recorded prior to change
- action: e.g., role.assign, role.revoke, delegation.create, policy.update
- resource_type: role|policy|service-account|key
- resource_id: canonical resource id (role name, policy id)
- before_state: short summary of role/policy before change (stringified diffs allowed)
- after_state: summary after change
- decision: allow|deny|conditional
- decision_reason: policy engine explanation / rule id
- client_ip, user_agent, geo
- auth_method: SSO|PAT|api-key|oidc
- exec_context: if triggered by automation, include automation_job_id
- ingestion_ts: when log arrived in central log store

Note: These field names map 1:1 to our SIEM field ingest pipeline; when querying add both original_event.* and normalized.* prefixes depending on the index.

Investigation playbook (first 2 hours):
- Step A: Rapid queries (use these as starting points)
  Splunk (examples):
    index=rbac_audit (event_ts>_relative_time("-48h")) request_id="<id>" OR actor_id="<actor>" | table event_ts, request_id, actor_id, action, resource_id, before_state, after_state, exec_context
  Elastic/Kibana DSL (examples):
    GET /rbac-audit/_search?q=actor_id:"user@example.com" AND event_ts: [now-48h TO now]&size=100
  NOTE: When searching for automation provenance, filter exec_context.automation_job_id or lookup job-runner logs.

- Step B: Confirm scope
  - Enumerate all role binding changes by request_id chain.
  - Identify any other actors that used the same request_id or the same automation_job_id.
  - Map affected resources (list roles, policies, service accounts) and downstream services that accept those roles.

- Step C: Containment re-check
  - If discovery reveals additional role grants, escalate containment: revoke auto-granted roles and roll out emergency-deny policy across affected projects/tenants.
  - If automation is responsible, pause/roll back the automation run (set automation-runner to paused and tag run id).

Evidence automation triggers and expectations:
- The evidence-collector Lambda (or equivalent worker) should be invoked with incident id. It must gather:
  - raw audit log slices for time window [t0-2h, t0+2h] (t0 = first alert timestamp), exported as ndjson to s3://redwood-evidence/<incident-id>/audit-raw.ndjson
  - normalized CSV containing the RBAC schema fields (see above) to s3://redwood-evidence/<incident-id>/rbac-normalized.csv
  - SIEM correlation export (search id or job id) and a screenshot of the alert rule that fired
  - snapshots of relevant control-plane configs (role definitions, policy templates) as text files with SHA256 checksums
- Automation run must create a ledger file (chain-of-custody.txt) listing actions, actor, timestamp, and the object created (path + sha256), signed by the evidence-collector service account.

Manual evidence checklist if automation unavailable:
- Export audit-index slices from the last 7 days covering actor_id and request_id.
- Take screenshots of SIEM alert and rule configuration.
- Run gcloud/az/aws iam list-role-policies --role=<role> and save output.
- Export token/session logs for the actor (session start/stop, IPs).
- Create chain-of-custody.txt and note all manual steps.

SIEM export and ingestion notes:
- Prefer bulk NDJSON exports over CSV when including nested objects (before_state diffs).
- Tag exports with metadata: incident_id, exported_by, export_time_utc, query_hash.
- Our SIEM ingestion pipeline tags fields with normalized.* and original.*; always include both in evidence packages.
- For long retention exports to legal/compliance, use encryption-at-rest + KMS key id and record key_id in chain-of-custody.

Forensics: quick triage heuristics
- If decision_reason references policy rule 'delegation.auto-approve', treat as automation-origin and prioritize stopping automation.
- If actor authenticated via SSO and mfa=false, look for any concurrent SSO token anomalies (sso-token-refresh spikes).
- If mass-grants appear (N>5 role.assign in 10m), suspect runaway automation or compromised service account.

When to escalate to Incident Response (IR)
- Evidence of lateral movement or data exfiltration.
- Privilege grants that open access to production data stores.
- External disclosure or legal hold requests.

Communications (templates):
- Initial page (Slack): [INC-<id>] Possible RBAC V2 anomaly: suspected delegation spike affecting 4 projects. IC: @username. Evidence owner: @username. Containment actions taken: emergency-deny applied. Next update in 15m.
- External customer notification: draft with privacy/compliance vetted wording; do not send without CISO or legal sign-off.

Postmortem template (use after incident is stable and evidence preserved)
- Title: concise summary (e.g., "RBAC V2: unintended auto-delegation caused mass role grants")
- Incident ID: INC-<id>
- Timeline (UTC) - bulletized events with timestamps
- Root cause hypothesis (short)
- Confirmed root cause (after investigation)
- Contributing factors (systems, human, procedural)
- Impact summary (services, customers, data scope)
- Detection: how was this first detected (SIEM rule, pager, internal report)
- Containment & remediation actions taken (chronological)
- Evidence snapshot locations (S3 paths, SIEM export ids)
- Long-term mitigations: code/config changes, policy changes, monitoring rules to add
- Rollback/compensation steps if applicable
- Lessons learned and assigned action items (owner + due date)
- Compliance/legal notes (preserved for legal if needed)
- Postmortem severity rating and closure date

Example postmortem action items (realistic):
- Disable delegation.auto-approve by default; require manual approval flow for new delegations (owner: Priya K.; due: 2025-03-01)
- Add SIEM rule to detect >3 role.assign by same actor in 10m with severity=high (owner: Marcus H.; due: 2025-02-28)
- Harden evidence-collector to include automation job run graphs in export (owner: Lina G.; due: 2025-03-15)

Appendix A — Useful search snippets
- Find automation-runner invocations by job id (Elasticsearch):
  GET /automation-runner-logs/_search?q=job_id:"<job-id>"&size=100
- Correlate request_id to downstream API calls (Splunk):
  index=apilogs request_id="<request_id>" | stats count by endpoint, status

Appendix B — Chain-of-custody example (format)
- Incident: INC-2025-0001
- Evidence collector run: ec-2025-0001
- Item: audit-raw.ndjson, path: s3://redwood-evidence/INC-2025-0001/audit-raw.ndjson, sha256: <hex>, collected_by: evidence-collector@redwood-infra, collected_at: 2025-02-09T18:22:03Z
- Notes: automated export; original index snapshot id: idx-8792

Appendix C — Recovery checklist (post containment)
- Validate emergency-deny removal process: run dry-run apply against staging and verify expected role states.
- Reconcile any legitimate grants that were revoked during containment and reapply with multi-person approval.
- Run regression checks on delegation automation to ensure the fix prevents re-occurrence.

Notes and open questions (to record as part of postmortem):
- Do we have sufficient telemetry on pre- and post-policy evaluations to reconstruct decision_reason in 100% of cases?
- Should evidence-collector automatically notify Legal for incidents with >1 person-data-scope affected?
- Are our SIEM retention and export pipelines certified for legal hold across APAC regions?

End of document.
